pattern.top_pattern: Rare inpatient and neuro cases are producing high-cost outliers
pattern.what_is_impacting: Rare IP Med/Surg and NF cases in CA / GA / NY / UNATTRIBUTED
key_driver_codes: Degenerative Nervous System Disorders without MCC
Other Disorders of Nervous System without CC/MCC
pattern.pattern_details: A set of rare inpatient and NF cases is creating meaningful spend through a small number of very expensive neurologic and medical admissions. These are not broad utilization trends; they are low-frequency, high-cost outliers, and several also carry missing or blank procedure information. The right response is combined clinical validation and case management, not broad utilization restriction.
pattern.why_it_matters: Rare high-cost cases can distort trend reading and require different action than routine inpatient growth.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Send these IP Med/Surg and NF cases to clinical and data-quality review to confirm true catastrophic complexity versus miscoding or missing procedures, then case-manage any repeat episodes.
pattern.validation_reason: The pattern is driven by low-volume high-cost cases with repeated unmapped or blank procedure fields.
evidence_summary: CA / NY / UNATTRIBUTED IP Med/Surg outliers added about $256K, including single cases of about $75.5K and $60.4K.
CA NF outliers added about $177K, led by G20C and I69354 cases of about $59.6K and $58.7K.
GA IP Med/Surg outliers added about $106K, led by R5381 and G959 cases.
GA NF outliers added about $45K on a handful of low-volume cases.
